*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health
emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 (https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City
Council Meeting of March 2, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
  electronically for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at
  athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative
  Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00
  A.M. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
  number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and
  agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to the close of the public
  hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the
  Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments:
  Members of the public can participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make
  comments noting the following:

  l The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join
  the conference 5 minutes prior.
  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception.
  Calls from landline phones are highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing
  the phone line, it is requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is
  delayed from the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making public
  comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to feedback.
  l Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 using the specific access codes detailed
  below for the respective City Council Dates:
  ¡ March 2, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#
  ¡ March 9, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#
  ¡ March 16, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#
  ¡ March 23, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#
  ¡ March 30, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your
  cable provider for details.
   ¡  March 30, 2021 – Access Code: 5914683#

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your
  cable provider for details.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and
listen to the meeting; however, members of the public who wish to orally address the
Legislative Body must use the public access options 1 and 2 noted above.
ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in
appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of
the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and
regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any person who requires a disability-
related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe and/or
offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or
service by contacting the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at 310-
412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301
or via email to aphillips@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than
24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting

Inglewood, California
  March 2, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  March 2, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and
  Parking Authority at the hour of 2:03 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Parking
  Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Parking Authority Chairman Butts, Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members/Parking Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Parking Authority officials and personnel
  present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Parking Authority Chairman Butts inquired if
  there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Parking Authority on any item on the Agendas.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos. CSA-
  2, DR-1, H-2, and P-1.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Dotson that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  February 26, 2021, in the amount of $3,116,807.29 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letter from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claim filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) Carmen Roberts for alleged personal injury; fell into SCE vault lid on February 4,
  2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Padilla that the
  City Council does hereby reject claim listed as A1. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  1
 101  AGREEMENT NO. 21-106 APPROVED – ELLISON WILSON ADVOCACY,
  LLC. Staff report dated March 2, 2021, was presented recommending approval of a
  three-year agreement with Ellison Wilson Advocacy, LLC, to provide legislative
  advocacy services for the City.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 21-106 in an annual amount
  not to exceed $63,000 (total contract amount not to exceed $189,000). The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO GRANT AGREEMENT NO. 920000000TOD201512
  APPROVED  -  LOS  ANGELES  COUNTY  METROPOLITAN
  TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY. Staff report dated March 2, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 1 to Grant Agreement No.
  920000000TOD201512 between the City of Inglewood and the Los Angeles County
  Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) for the Florence/Hindry and Crenshaw
  Station Transit Overlay District Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to Grant Agreement No.
  920000000TOD201512. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  PURCHASE ORDER AUTHORIZED – CROSSTOWN ELECTRICAL & DATA.
  Staff report dated March 2, 2021, was presented recommending approval of a purchase
  order with Crosstown Electrical & Data, Inc., for LED traffic control devices, per Bid
  No. RFB-0126.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve purchase order in the amount of $87,550. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 21-107 APPROVED –
  MICHAEL BAKER INTERNATIONAL, INC. Staff report dated March 2, 2021, was
  presented recommending award of a contract and approval of an agreement with Michael
  Baker International, Inc., to prepare the Urban Water Management Plan (UWMP) 2020
  study and the state-required plan/report to be submitted to the California Department of
  Water Resources (DWR).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 21-107 in
  an amount not to exceed $59,669.50 (includes a 10% contingency of $5,424.50), per Bid
  No. RFP #PW20200922. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

125  AGREEMENT NOS. 21-108/21-108A/21-108B/21-108D APPROVED – KANE,
  BALLMER & BERKMAN (“SPECIAL COUNSEL”). Staff report dated March 2,
  2021, was presented recommending approval of an agreement with Kane, Ballmer &
  Berkman (“Special Counsel”) for legal advice, guidance, and representation.

  It was moved by Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority
  Member/Parking Authority Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member/Parking Authority Member
  Padilla that the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Parking Authority

  2
   does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement Nos. 21-108/21-108A/21-108B/21-108D in the total
  amount of $500,000; and 2) Approve payment of outstanding invoices in an amount not
  to exceed $400,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council  Members/Successor  Agency  Members/Housing  Authority
  Members/Parking Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and
  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, reported the Special
  Primary Election today for Senate District 30 and the polling locations where residents
  can cast their votes. She spoke about National Women’s History Month beginning in
  March and paid homage to Stacey Abrams.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on his concerns about viewing the City Council
  Meeting on television. He addressed the Super Bowl that’s coming to Inglewood in 10
  months, and questioned what happened to the Boys and Girls Club.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in honor of Kelley Malone, niece of Henry and Rachel Brown, who left behind
  2 children and 3 grandchildren at the hour of 2:26 p.m.

  Approved this 27th day of July, 2021

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
